reviewed_source_excerpts: [F6] [[def-complex-exponential]] and [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]] define the exponential and give its addition law and real extension. [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]] gives $|e^{x+iy}|=e^x$; [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] gives its derivative and continuity. [[thm-ftc-second-part]] evaluates the continuous real and imaginary derivatives of its antiderivative on finite intervals.

4.1 For $R>0$, the derivative and componentwise FTC in [F6] give $\int_0^R e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}dt=(1-e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)R})/(\gamma-i\omega)$. The modulus formula gives $|e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)R}|=e^{-\gamma R}\to0$ and $|e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}|=e^{-\gamma t}$, whose integral is finite. Thus the stationary covariance is integrable. By evenness, $$S(\omega)=\frac V\pi\operatorname{Re}\int_0^\infty e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}dt =\frac V\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac1{\gamma-i\omega} =\frac{V\gamma}{\pi(\gamma^2+\omega^2)}.$$ The integral converges absolutely because $\gamma>0$. [A2, F6, step 3.2]

aliases.primary_location: Statement, strong-continuity claim; Proof step 3.1, where the proof takes Λ → I.
reviewed_source_excerpts:
Assume Countable Choice. On the future null cone write $p=(\omega,\mathbf k)$, $\omega=|\mathbf k|$, $\mathbf k\ne0$, and use the measure $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$. The fiber $p^\perp/\mathbb Cp$ has the positive quotient form of [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]]. Give the proper orthochronous Lorentz group its matrix topology: the subspace topology inherited from $\mathbb R^{16}$ with Euclidean matrix norm $\|A\|_{\rm mat}=(\sum_{i,j=0}^3|A_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$. For each proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$, the action
$$[s(p)]\longmapsto[\Lambda s(\Lambda^{-1}p)]$$
is a unitary representation on the square-integrable quotient sections. It is strongly continuous for this topology, meaning $\|U_\Lambda s-U_{\Lambda_0}s\|\to0$ for every section $s$ as $\|\Lambda-\Lambda_0\|_{\rm mat}\to0$. Its bosonic Fock lift is strongly continuous for the same topology. Under the unitary identification with $\mathcal H_T$ given by
$T_p[\epsilon]:=\boldsymbol\epsilon-(\mathbf k/\omega)\epsilon^0$
and $u(\mathbf k)=T_p[s(p)]/\sqrt{2\omega}$, as in [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]], the free translation representation for $a=(a^0,\mathbf a)\in\mathbb R^4$ has phase $e^{i(\omega a^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a)}$. Its bosonic Fock lift has the joint PVM $\mathsf E$ whose $n$-particle sector acts by multiplication by $\mathbf1_{\{(\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|,-\sum_{r=1}^n\mathbf k_r)\in B\}}$ for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^4$; on the vacuum it acts by $\mathbf1_B(0)$. Define its joint spectrum to be
$$\operatorname{supp}(\mathsf E):=\{q\in\mathbb R^4:\mathsf E(U)\ne0\text{ for every open neighborhood }U\text{ of }q\}.$$
Then this joint spectrum is the closed future cone
$$\overline V_+=\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\},$$
with the vacuum at $(0,\mathbf0)$. In the product realization of the sectors in [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]], on sector $n$ the energy operator multiplies by $\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|$ and has the exact maximal domain
$$D(H_E)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(\mathbb R^3)^n}\left(\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|\right)^2\|\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)\|^2\,d^3\mathbf k_1\cdots d^3\mathbf k_n<\infty\right\},$$
with the vacuum component unrestricted; here $\Psi_n$ is the symmetric transverse wavefunction in the product realization and the norm is the product-fiber Hilbert norm. Each momentum operator $P_j$ multiplies by $-\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}$ and has maximal domain
$$D(P_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(\mathbb R^3)^n}\left|\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}\right|^2\|\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)\|^2\,d^3\mathbf k_1\cdots d^3\mathbf k_n<\infty\right\},$$
again with unrestricted vacuum component. These are mathematical free-field representation statements.

Matrix multiplication is continuous, and the Lorentz equation gives $\Lambda^{-1}=\eta\Lambda^T\eta$, so inversion is continuous in the stated matrix topology. For $v\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ with support in $B_R$, $R\ge1$, take the four-component representative $s_v(p)=(0,\sqrt{2\omega}\,P_T(\mathbf k)v(\mathbf k))$; under the stated unitary identification its class corresponds to $u=P_Tv\in\mathcal H_T$. Put $q=\Lambda^{-1}p$ and $a_\Lambda(\mathbf k)=T_p\Lambda(0,\sqrt{2q^0}\,P_T(\mathbf q)v(\mathbf q))$, the transverse chart representative of the transformed quotient section. If $\Lambda$ is sufficiently close to $I$, uniformly for future null $p$ one has $\omega/2\le q^0=|\mathbf q|\le2\omega$ and $\|\Lambda\|_{m op}\le2$: use $\|p\|_2=\sqrt2\omega$, the displayed inverse formula and the Euclidean Cauchy–Schwarz bound for a matrix acting on a vector. Thus $a_\Lambda$ vanishes outside $B_{2R}$, and $\|T_p\|_{m op}\le\sqrt2$, $\|P_T\|_{m op}\le1$ give $|a_\Lambda(\mathbf k)|\le C M\sqrt\omega$, where $M=\sup|v|$ and $C$ is independent of sufficiently small $\Lambda-I$. Consequently $|a_\Lambda-a_I|$ is bounded by a fixed constant $C_R M$ on the common support. Its squared $L^2(d
u)$ contribution on $B_\delta$ is at most $C_R^2M^2
u(B_\delta)=C_R^2M^2\pi\delta^2$ by [F6, F10]. On the annulus $\delta\le|\mathbf k|\le2R$, extend the explicit formula to matrices $A$ in a sufficiently small closed Euclidean matrix box about $I$ by putting $q=\eta A^T\eta p$. On that box $q^0$ and $|\mathbf q|$ remain positive, bounded away from zero on the annulus; the formula using $P_T(\mathbf q)=I-(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|)(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|)^T$ is therefore continuous. The box times annulus is closed bounded in $\mathbb R^{19}$, hence compact, and [F11] gives uniform continuity of this formula there. Restricting back to Lorentz matrices yields $a_\Lambda	o a_I$ uniformly on the annulus, which has finite $
u$-measure by [F6]. First choose $\delta$, then $\Lambda-I$, to obtain $\|a_\Lambda-a_I\|_{L^2(d
u)}	o0$; this is exactly the quotient-section norm. No fiber value at the omitted apex is used. These sections are dense by [F4, F7]: approximate any $u\in\mathcal H_T$ by smooth compactly supported $v$ and project by $P_T$. Unitarity from step 2.1 gives $\|U_\Lambda s-s\|\le2\|s-s_v\|+\|U_\Lambda s_v-s_v\|$, extending continuity to every section. At any $\Lambda_0$, the representation identity reduces continuity to $U_{\Lambda_0^{-1}\Lambda}	o I$, and $\Lambda_0^{-1}\Lambda	o I$ in the matrix topology. For an elementary $n$-tensor, telescoping and unitarity give $\|(U_\Lambda^{\otimes n}-I)(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_n)\|\le\sum_{j=1}^n\|(U_\Lambda-I)h_j\|\prod_{l
e j}\|h_l\|	o0$. Finite linear combinations are dense in the Hilbert tensor product; the symmetric projection is a contraction commuting with the tensor action, so continuity holds on each symmetric sector. The vacuum is fixed. Truncating an arbitrary Fock vector to finitely many sectors leaves an error bounded by twice its tail norm under these unitary maps; letting that tail tend to zero proves strong continuity on all Fock space.

Suppose $f:\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d	imes I	o(0,\infty)$ is $C^1$ in space and time and $C^2$ in velocity. Fix a positive constant reference density $f_{m ref}$ with the same units as $f$, and put $\ell(r,v,t)=\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{m ref})$. For each $t\in I$, assume $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\ell|$ are integrable over $\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d$. For every compact interval $I_0\subset I$, assume there is a nonnegative $G_{I_0}\in L^1(\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d,dr\,dv)$ such that $|(1+\ell)\partial_t f|\le G_{I_0}$ almost everywhere for every $t\in I_0$. Also assume $(1+|\ell|)|v\cdot
abla_r f|\in L^1(\Omega	imes\mathbb R^d,dr\,dv)$ for each $t\in I$. Write $A=f(r,v,t)f(r,w,t)$ and $B=f(r,v',t)f(r,w',t)$. For each $t\in I$, assume $r\mapsto\int_{Q_{m el}}|(A-B)(\ell(r,v,t)+\ell(r,w,t)-\ell(r,v',t)-\ell(r,w',t))|\,d
u$ is measurable and belongs to $L^1(\Omega,dr)$. Let $Q$ and the symmetric collision measure $
u$ satisfy the weak identity in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]] for tests $1$ and $\ell(r,\cdot,t)$ at each $(r,t)$, with absolute convergence, and suppose
$$\partial_t f+v\cdot
abla_r f=Q(f).$$
Then for $H[f](t)=\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\ell\,dv\,dr$,
$$ rac{d}{dt}H[f](t)=- rac14\int_\Omega\int_{Q_{m el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d
u\,dr\le0.$$
The integrand is nonnegative because $\log$ is strictly increasing. Equality in the entropy-production integral holds exactly when $A=B$ for $
u$-almost every collision at almost every $r$. Under the additional assumptions that $
u$ is locally finite, has full support on $Q_{m el}$, and $f$ is positive and $C^2$ in $v$, this balance implies for almost every $r$ that
$$\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{m ref})=\alpha(r,t)+b(r,t)\cdot v+ rac{\lambda(r,t)}2|v|^2.$$
If $f(r,\cdot,t)$ is integrable over $\mathbb R^d$, then $\lambda(r,t)<0$, so its velocity profile is Maxwellian. Conversely, every profile of this form has zero collision entropy production. The weak collision identity is an explicit model hypothesis; this is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a PDE existence theorem.

4.1 Under [A3], fix an $r$ for which collision balance holds $\nu$-almost everywhere. The function $(v,w,v',w')\mapsto A-B$ is continuous. If it were nonzero at an allowed collision, it would remain nonzero on a relative open neighborhood; full support of $\nu$ gives that neighborhood positive measure, contradicting balance. Hence balance holds for every elastic collision. The set of such $r$ has full Lebesgue measure and is dense in $\Omega$; continuity in $r$ extends the identity to any limit point when needed. [A1, A3, F1, step 3.1, algebra]

Assume the Axiom of Choice. On $\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}$ let $u(x)=1/(16\pi^4|x|^4)$, equivalently the square of the displayed Euclidean kernel $C_0(x)=1/(4\pi^2|x|^2)$; interpret $u$ as its regular distribution there. Choose $\chi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$ equal to one near $0$. For $\mu>0$ define

$$T_\mu(\varphi):=\int_{\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}}\frac{\varphi(x)-\chi(\mu x)\varphi(0)}{16\pi^4|x|^4}\,d^4x.$$

Then $T_\mu$ is a distribution extending $u$, has scaling degree $4$, and for every $\mu,\nu>0$,

$$T_\mu-T_\nu=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\log(\mu/\nu)\,\delta_0.$$

In particular, no extension of $u$ with scaling degree $4$ is exactly homogeneous, where exact homogeneity means $\rho^4T_\rho=T$ for every $\rho>0$. Coordinates use one fixed Euclidean unit; if units are assigned, $\mu$ and $\nu$ have reciprocal coordinate units, so the logarithm's ratio is dimensionless. This is a Euclidean distribution identity and does not identify a measured coupling or physical beta function.
